title: Broken Scale Invariance and One‐Reversal Witnesses of Non‐Passivity for Fractional Creep Elements of Order Above Two in Rock Rheology
content: Fractional creep elements σ = ξ Dβε of order above one are fitted to tertiary rock creep on tests in which the stress keeps one sign, and orders above two, the non-passive band, occur in a published granite model. The absorbed work is a quadratic form in the stress history. It is non-negative on the cone of one-sign histories for every β ≥ 0, yet for β &gt; 2 it is not positive semidefinite, so non-passivity can be exposed only by reversing the stress. One reversal suffices: for every β &gt; 2 and every ratio of durations, a closed-form interval of reversal amplitudes gives negative work, as three-point instances of Schoenberg’s variogram condition. A single power-law element is scale invariant, so these witnesses exist at every duration. Two power-law branches of different order break this invariance: two-level single-reversal witnesses exist only above κ(β1, β2) tc, where tc is their crossover time, and κ has a closed-form bound. For a granite model of tertiary order 13.605, held active under reversed stress, the two-level horizon is 78.55 h = 1.0812 tc; a one-reversal history with more stress levels exposes it at 68 h, within the published record.
